Kymone Freeman

DC Statehood Green candidate for Delegate to the House of Representatives from the District of Columbia · Open seat

Playwright, community activist, and co-founder of We Act Radio

Kymone Freeman is a native Washingtonian, playwright, community activist, and co-founder of We Act Radio, a radio and TV studio in D.C. He was the DC Statehood Green Party's nominee for D.C. Delegate in 2024, when he received 7.0% of the vote. He ran unopposed in the party's June 16, 2026 primary and is on the D.C. Board of Elections' list of November 3, 2026 general election candidates as the Statehood Green nominee.

Where Freeman stands

D.C. statehood and Home Rule
His campaign slogan is "No Representation, No Taxes." He proposes pushing for statehood through "direct economic action" and says, "If we don't have a voice, they don't get our money."
Federal taxes / representation
Supports federal income tax resistance by D.C. residents as a way to push for statehood. Says past delegates did not deliver statehood or voting rights.
Public safety
Calls crime and poverty "symptoms of systemic neglect." Proposes investing in jobs and mental health and ending the school-to-prison pipeline.
Housing affordability
Wants city budgets that put housing, health care, and education ahead of policing and displacement.
Economy and jobs
Proposes shifting the city's priorities "from corporate handouts to community investment."
